profile.name: Mike Layton
profile.bio: Toronto city councillor 2010–2022 who did not seek re-election in 2022 and became York University’s chief sustainability officer in March 2023; son of former federal NDP leader Jack Layton.

promises.text: Expand resources for community land trusts, non-profit and supportive housing, and require real affordability in new development on public land.
Prioritize Ward 11 development applications that include affordable housing.
Fully fund the rent bank and eviction protection program.
Institute a Speculation Watch List for renovictions and rental replacement.
Have City inspections and repairs step in earlier in chronically deficient buildings.
Advocate for stronger Landlord and Tenant Board enforcement and for reinstatement and expansion of rent control.
Support weekly TTC fare capping and expand fare capping.
Expand school breakfast programs and bring universal lunch to all schools by 2030.
Expand food nutrition programs in City camps.
Uphold and update the City's fair wage policy.
Scale up building retrofit programs and Building Emissions Performance Standards.
Build a green jobs pipeline for youth.
Pause data-centre approvals until a City framework is in place.
Bring in a maximum-temperature bylaw for rental units, expand the free air-conditioning/heat-pump program, and update the Heat Relief Strategy yearly.
Create a street-tree resiliency strategy and grow the tree-planting budget.
Increase flood-infrastructure funding (Green Streets) and introduce a stormwater charge on large paved parking lots.
Oppose incineration and cut single-use items.
Finish the cycling network, defend bike lanes, and implement the Cycling Network Plan.
Add more RapidTO priority on College Street and Dundas West.
Expand the crisis-worker pilot on Line 1.
Fight the provincial rollback of automated speed enforcement.
Create a City-led snow-shovelling program.
Oppose Island airport expansion.
Keep park washrooms open year-round, including Christie Pits and Bellevue Square.
Review the Astral street-furniture and garbage contract.
Expand community-based crisis response.
Office commitment on his plan page: answer constituent inquiries within 24 hours and publish an annual progress report-back.

expensesDetailSource.publisher: City Clerk's Office, City of Toronto
expensesDetailSource.note: Figures are the City's routine disclosure of constituency services and office expenses, shown as published, by category, from 2013. This is a separate publication from the annual remuneration reports in expenses.json, with a narrower scope — office spending only, not pay, benefits or staff salaries — and the two are never added together. Amounts shown as personal funds are the member's own money, as the City reports it. Invoice-level documents stay on the City's site; category amounts link to them.
